title: Snapshot restoration drops executable permissions and links
reasoning: Archive creation preserves file modes and can store symbolic or hard links, but restoration only reads regular-file contents and writes new files with default permissions. Executable scripts lose their execute bits, and archived links disappear. Workspace preparation/reset and checkpoint export therefore change runnable filesystem state despite preserving ordinary file bytes.
reproduction: Snapshot a directory containing an executable script and a symbolic link to a regular file, then extract into a fresh directory. The script is no longer executable and the link is absent.
recommendation: Restore supported filesystem entry types and executable permissions using a containment-safe extraction policy. Explicitly reject unsupported entries instead of silently dropping them.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Included snapshot-backed workspace tests verify ordinary file existence and text contents, without permission or link round-trip assertions.
suggestedRegressionTest: Expand workspace snapshot round-trip scenarios to executable files and safe relative links, checking equivalent behavior after prepare and reset.
minimumFixScope: Snapshot archive restoration and filesystem metadata handling.
